# v1.1.0-dev.84 — Select many windows at once, and a display editor that got out of its own way

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.83`.

## Select Several Windows, Change Them Together

The visual editor only ever had one window selected. Moving six windows to
another monitor meant opening six editors.

It works the way selecting files works now:

- **Click** picks one.
- **Ctrl+click** adds or removes one, leaving the rest alone.
- **Shift+click** takes everything between what you clicked and where you
  started.
- **Ctrl+Shift+click** adds a whole run to what you already had.

Shift deliberately measures from where you started rather than from the
last thing you touched. A second Shift+click therefore shrinks the same
range instead of walking it along. Ranges run in the order the windows
appear on screen.

With more than one selected, the strip under the canvas stops describing a
window and starts offering what makes sense for a group: **move to
monitor**, **set state**, and **remove**.

Position and size are deliberately not on that list. One X applied to
twelve windows stacks all twelve in the same place, which is never what
anyone meant by changing their settings together.

## Resolutions Read The Same Way Either Way Up

A rotated monitor listed its sizes backwards. A 2560 × 1440 panel stood on
its end reported every mode as 1440 × 2560, because that is how Windows
reports them once a display is turned. The list read like nonsense.

Sizes are written long side first now, whichever way the panel is facing.
What gets sent to Windows is unchanged, because that half has to stay in
the orientation Windows is speaking.

There is one deliberate exception. A display offering both shapes at once
keeps the true order, since flattening it there would make 1920 × 1080 and
1080 × 1920 read identically.

## Find A Resolution By Typing

Some displays offer over two hundred modes. There is a filter box beside
the list now, appearing once the list is long enough to be worth one.

It goes on the numbers, because nobody agrees on the separator and the list
itself uses a × that is not on your keyboard. Type `1440` and you get every
mode with 1440 on either side. Type `2560 1440` or `2560x1440` and you get
that one. Type `25 14` and you get it just as well. A word rather than a
number searches the labels, so `largest` finds the row marked that way.

Whatever you already had selected stays in the list while you type. A
filter that hides your own value is worse than no filter.

## The Display Editor Got Out Of Its Own Way

Six same-looking buttons ran along the bottom. Three of them are gone from
there:

- **History** and **Restore defaults**, which used to be "Remove display
  step", moved up beside the heading. They act on the whole display step
  rather than on the edit you are in the middle of.
- **Add resolutions** went the other way, down into the resolution row. It
  is about which sizes a display offers, which is where it belongs.

The bottom row is Apply now, Cancel and Save.

Two controls went away entirely. **Include small sizes** is gone. Every
size the driver reports is simply listed. Hiding the small ones behind a
checkbox meant that the one time you wanted 1024 × 768 you had to know the
checkbox existed. **By hand** is gone too. A saved size your display cannot
currently do still shows up as one, which keeps a setting that is
configured but unavailable from looking like nothing at all.

The tips under the monitor picture sit in a box of their own now, centred,
with room above and below.

## Dialogs Fill Their Windows

Every dialog is its own window. Its content was still sizing itself as
though it were floating over the app. A list that was already scrolling
could sit above a band of empty window.

Headings and button rows pin to the top and bottom now. Whatever scrolls
between them takes the room that is left. That covers Saved versions in
the History dialog and every panel shaped like it.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
